title: Scope & local Mistakes
summary: Declaring locals inside blocks makes them invisible outside; forgetting `local` creates globals; shadowing re-declares a name and the old value silently survives elsewhere. Most 'variable not updating' bugs are scope bugs.

explanation.whatItIs: Where a name lives decides who sees it — and whether updates hit the variable you think they hit.
explanation.whyItExists: Lexical scope keeps big programs sane; the sharp edges show when declarations and uses land in different blocks.
symptoms: Counter 'resets' — you re-declared it inside a loop/function
Two counters: one updated, one read (shadowing)
Strict mode complaining about globals from missing `local`
explanation.fix: Declare at the WIDEST scope that needs it; always write `local`; rename when shadowing by accident; enable strict mode.
tips: Hoist state up: local score = 0 BEFORE the loop that updates it
Luau's --!strict helps catch scope slips at edit time
commonMistakes: local x = 0 inside a function called repeatedly → always 0
if blocks creating throwaway locals you expected to persist
Shadowing a parameter with a same-named local inside

examples.title: Reset vs hoisted
examples.code:
-- ❌ Resets every call:
local function onHit()
    local hits = 0        -- fresh zero every time
    hits += 1
    print(hits)           -- always 1
end

-- ✅ Hoisted:
local hits = 0
local function onHitSafe()
    hits += 1
    print(hits)           -- 1, 2, 3…
end

-- Shadowing trap:
local mode = "walk"
do
    local mode = "run"    -- NEW variable, dies with the block
    print(mode)           --> run
end
print(mode)               --> walk (unchanged!)
